summary: Academica's programmes are practice-oriented. Assessing applied science work takes assessors who understand both the theory and the practice, and that combination is scarce. New assessors need assessment competence, and training them takes time and money. Marking currently costs Academica €32,400 a year. Formative feedback on drafts takes a week, a summative assessment four weeks.

Eduface is an educational AI model that gives formative and summative feedback on student assignments, inside NEO LMS. Students hand in as they always do, and grades and feedback sync back to NEO. Teachers read, adjust and release every grade. The goal for Academica is to be able to give feedback at any time: assessing more efficiently, faster and more accurately, with fewer external assessors hired in. This is a concrete step in the efficiency theme of Academica's course plan to 2030.

Our mutual aim is to go live in NEO LMS with the first programmes once the test morning has confirmed the two requirements: a working NEO LMS connection, and good feedback on practice-oriented assignments. This document is the shared plan to get there, and both teams keep it up to date.

days: Teachers and programme managers run real practice-oriented assignments through Eduface inside NEO LMS and judge the feedback on their own material. qa: Are the LMS connection and fitting the model to our rubrics charged on top?
No. Both are included in the price per student.
Can we use the SURF data processing agreement?
No, since Academica is not publicly funded. We work with Academica's own data processing agreement instead.
How does billing work when student numbers go up and down?
We invoice monthly, in advance, based on the number of active students in NEO LMS that month. The minimum of €1,500 covers the first 400 students.
Do the LTI settings have to be filled in again for every course?
No. Eduface is configured once, centrally, in NEO LMS. An Eduface assignment in the course template is copied into every new course, as NEO Support confirmed.
Can a thesis go straight to the student?
No. Teachers read, adjust and release every grade. For the thesis the four-eyes route applies, so the grade stays on hold until it is released.
